sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid bita1251 and its 7 attached references (Blench 2016, Blench 2006, Koops 1971, Meek 1931 x2, Williamson & Shimizu 1968, Williamson 1973).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: every reference is listed by Glottolog as a wordlist/overview/ethnographic; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Angitso, Michael Terhemen & Roland Kießling. 2024. Towards reconstructing the numeral classifier system of Proto-Tivoid. Afrika und Übersee 97: 204-232. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.329
sources.note: Nothing; p.206 states Tiv and Ugare 'are the only Tivoid languages for which sufficient data is presently available' — no Bitare data.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97: 1-46. Hamburg University Press. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288 (CC-BY).
sources.note: Name only; no phonological information on Bitare.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: KWEF. Entry 50 Bitare.
sources.note: Nothing; references for Bitare = 'Wordlist: Shimizu (1981)' only.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. The Tivoid languages. Handout, Bantu VI conference, Helsinki.
sources.note: Nothing; Bitare [=Njwande] listed with population and source (Koops ms.) only.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3 (p.2): 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only three languages, Tiv, Esimbi and Ugarə'; Tiv and Ugare described as two-tone languages. Njwande appears only as a wordlist column (Koops ms.).

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2013. Ethnologue, 17th ed., entry Bitare [brt] (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Nothing; 'Unwritten', similar to Abon; no typological notes.

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [1990]. Tivoid survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022.
sources.note: Nothing; Bitare/Njwande not covered (Cameroonian southern Tivoid only).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [printout 2010]. Wordlists of Abõ and Njwande languages spoken in southern Taraba State, Nigeria (data collected by R. Koops, 1970s). Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 13 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Only phonological remark (p.1): Koops' tone marks are unusable ('low tones are almost non-existent and high tones rare'), so the vertical-line diacritic was omitted; wordlists of Njwande (Akia, Kararuwa) plus Meek's 1931 Bitare forms.
